requests.purpose: Scenes s091 “One bad day” and s092 “Two different questions” (single): an illustrative difficult day that lets the essay separate a passing mood from a life going well.
requests.description: Fictional Bob seated beside an open, unlettered notebook. Tired eyebrows, small neutral mouth, relaxed shoulders; the task looks demanding without a despairing or triumphant verdict. One intact figure.
requests.alt: Bob sits tired beside an open notebook.

requests.purpose: Scenes s093 “Living well takes more than a mood” (single, after Koj's dialogue), s097 “Chosen challenge, forced hardship” (pair with A06, view label “Chosen effort”) and s100 “Who ranks pleasures?” (pair with A05, view label “Studying”): effort a person chooses, demanding and still worth it.
requests.description: Koj with the recognizable curl, compact seated body, open book and pencil. Concentrated eyebrows, slightly strained expression; no ecstatic smile, grades, labels or badges.
requests.alt: Koj concentrates on an open book with a pencil in hand.

requests.purpose: Scenes s094 “Having a say” and s108 “Choosing what to keep” (single, after Vier's dialogue): having a say over which demands to keep, without depicting a path or an idealized second self.
requests.description: Vier with angular tuft, thoughtful face, seated with a phone set down and a notebook nearby. One hand raised in a small questioning gesture; no pathways, arrows or idealized second self.
requests.alt: Vier pauses beside a phone and notebook with a questioning expression.

requests.purpose: Scenes s096 “A hobby can offer several things” (single) and s100 “Who ranks pleasures?” (pair with A03, view label “Playing”): a freely chosen hobby supplying competence, autonomy and relatedness at once.
requests.description: TJ and fictional Bob sit together with simple game controllers; relaxed expressive faces. One small unlettered screen off to the side, no game logo or generated UI. Preserve both full figures.
requests.alt: TJ and Bob enjoy playing a game together.

requests.purpose: Scene s097 “Chosen challenge, forced hardship” (pair with A03, view label “Required work”): obligation a fictional person cannot refuse, never assigned to Koj.
requests.description: Fictional Bob, visibly tired, seated with an unlettered stack of task papers and a simple clock. No bill amounts, grades, employer or hardship assigned to a member.
requests.alt: Bob looks tired beside a stack of tasks and a clock.

requests.purpose: Scene s098 “Rest does not need to pay us back” (single, after TJ's dialogue): rest shown as worth having in itself, with no timer, reward or productivity framing.
requests.description: TJ with crown tuft reclining comfortably against a simple cushion; restful eyes, small content smile. No phone app, timer, productivity badge or “before/after” body.
requests.alt: TJ rests comfortably against a cushion.

requests.purpose: Scene s103 “The expected life” (single): four expected milestones as separate blank props, leaving room for the browser labels “Grades”, “Career”, “Relationship” and “Income” beside the matching prop, with no sequence or score.
requests.description: Vier thoughtful at center; four separate small props around him: blank grade sheet, work bag, two-person keepsake silhouette, blank banknote. Plenty of blank space for the four browser labels specified in s103. No milestones route or scoring.
requests.alt: Vier considers symbols of grades, work, relationships and income.

requests.purpose: Scene s104 “What does the purchase give me?” (single, after TJ's dialogue) and the default “Connection” state of scene s105 “One phone, different uses”: the same phone used to stay close to someone.
requests.description: TJ using a small phone with a warm smile; fictional Bob beside him, holding a phone and smiling back. No screen lettering, messages, notification counts or connection arrows. Two full figures.
requests.alt: TJ and Bob smile while using their phones to connect.

requests.purpose: Second “Comparison” state of scene s105 “One phone, different uses”: the same phone and pose turned to comparison instead; framing must stay close to A09a so the optional control swaps states instantaneously.
requests.description: Same TJ identity and phone pose, now thoughtful and slightly tense; no second person, status symbols, numeric counts or assumed diagnosis. Preserve framing close to A09a for an instantaneous state swap.
requests.alt: TJ looks tense while looking at his phone.

requests.purpose: Scene s106 “Pressure to be cheerful” (single): sadness that persists while a fictional friend urges cheer, with clear space for the browser dialogue “Cheer up!” beside the friend rather than over heads.
requests.description: Sad fictional Bob, shoulders lowered, beside a second fictional friend making an encouraging hand gesture. Friend's face cheerful; Bob's sadness remains visible. Clear room for the browser text “Cheer up!” near friend, not over heads.
requests.alt: Bob looks sad while a cheerful friend gestures toward him.

requests.purpose: Scene s107 “Joy does not cancel the problem” (single): real enjoyment coexisting with unresolved demands, with neither read as the truer feeling.
requests.description: Fictional Bob seated with a plate of food and a phone placed aside. A restrained smile and worried brow coexist; a small stack of blank papers nearby indicates unresolved demands, not measured debt.
requests.alt: Bob enjoys a meal while nearby tasks remain unresolved.

requests.purpose: Scenes s109 “Ordinary care” and s111 “Sharing a meal” (group): the three members eating together as ordinary care, with browser names reserved above their heads.
requests.description: TJ, Koj and Vier seated around a small low table with three simple plates. Friendly, calm expressions, full visible heads and compact bodies. No restaurant brand, purchase or depicted real event. Reserve browser names above heads.
requests.alt: TJ, Koj and Vier share a meal around a small table.

requests.purpose: Scene s112 “Who keeps the relationship going?” (single): the unnoticed organizing work behind a shared meal, carried by a fictional person and never assigned to a member.
requests.description: One fictional organizer arranging plates while checking a blank phone. Focused rather than permanently unhappy; other guests need not appear. No gender-coded duty or inferred member household.
requests.alt: A fictional organizer arranges plates while checking a schedule.

requests.purpose: Scene s113 “Boundaries belong in connection” (single): chosen solitude as part of connection rather than a picture of loneliness.
requests.description: Fictional Bob reading alone, relaxed posture and content face; one simple book. Empty surrounding space stays transparent, without loneliness symbols.
requests.alt: Bob reads alone with a relaxed expression.

requests.purpose: Default “Time available” state of scene s114 “The same invitation, different options”: the same fictional person with hours free to accept an invitation.
requests.description: Fictional Bob standing freely with a small basketball, smiling and ready to join. No literal calendar, text or estimated free hours.
requests.alt: Bob has time to join a game.

requests.purpose: Second “Time claimed” state of scene s114 “The same invitation, different options”: the same identity with those hours already claimed by work and travel.
requests.description: Same Bob identity carrying a plain work bag, glancing at a clock, with a simple bus-stop post nearby. Tired expression; no employer, route map or fictional schedule data.
requests.alt: Bob carries a work bag beside a bus-stop post and clock.

requests.purpose: Scene s115 “Buying time moves the work” (pair, view labels “Time gained” then “Work performed”): bought time reappearing as someone else's labour; the pair layout needs two separately usable cutouts.
requests.description: Two fictional people in separate transparent groups: one resting, the other doing dishes. Distinguish through pose and browser labels, not a rich/poor caricature. Keep task tools fully visible. Supply separately usable cutouts for pair layout.
requests.alt: First cutout: A fictional person rests. Second cutout: A fictional worker does the dishes.

requests.purpose: Scenes s124 “Make room on campus” and s127 “Test a proposal before claiming success” (single): the fictional shared space our proposal asks for, with no real location named and no success marks.
requests.description: Fictional proposed shared space: bench, modest shade and two students spending time together, with clear unobstructed space alongside seating. No actual campus landmark, commercial branding or success indicators.
requests.alt: Two fictional students spend time in a shaded shared seating area.

requests.purpose: Scene s126 “Who benefits, who pays?” (pair, view labels “Students using the space” then “Staff maintaining it”): the maintenance the proposal creates; the pair layout needs two separately usable cutouts.
requests.description: Pair cutouts: two fictional students at a shared table; a fictional staff member cleaning the same kind of table. Staff expression attentive, not automatically miserable. No implication of measured workload.
requests.alt: First cutout: Two fictional students spend time at a shared table. Second cutout: A fictional staff member cleans a shared table.
